metadata.methods_description: Continuous EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz from 31 active Ag/AgCl electrodes (10/20 system, actiChamp Plus; ground FPz, online reference FCz). Participants completed a within-subject RDK left/right motion discrimination task with baseline, low-level prior and high-level prior conditions. Motion coherence was individualized with two QUEST staircases targeting 75% accuracy. Stimuli were presented with PsychoPy on a 240 Hz monitor at 65 cm viewing distance. Post-experimental questionnaires assessed manipulation checks, belief strength, psychosis proneness and psychological flexibility.

citation_details.title: Precision-weighted updating shows cross-task consistency as a bounded computational marker when precision gain is sufficiently large
citation_details.author: Ke Wan
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Background. Single-task fitted parameters are often treated as portable traits. We asked whether a precision-weighting coefficient γ in CPSP-8 generalizes across tasks under preregistered hierarchical transfer cross-validation (HTCV). Methods. Archived NUTS posteriors came from OpenNeuro BART (ds000030; N=173) and CCTHot (ds004636; N=104); HierPrior (ds008083; N=43) supplied a behavioural γ probe. Ornstein–Uhlenbec parameters were frozen. Consistency required a 95% HDI containing 0. Post-review checks (not used to change H1–H4) were ROPE, conjugate MAP+SE sensitivity, WAIC/LOO, age/sex IPW, and a non-null family-separability grid. Choice and RT RMSE were scored against dedicated models. Results. Only γ transferred under preregistered NUTS (BART–CCT 0.3835, 95% HDI [−0.0084, 0.7826]; all three HDIs contain 0). This is not ROPE equivalence and fails on a conjugate grid (0/36 cells contain 0). WAIC favoured task-specific γ. Other decision parameters failed H1. γ recovered at 960 trials (median r≈0.66) but was family-inseparable from RW at γ=0. Non-null probes separated at γ≥1.0 with ≥960 trials (or γ≥1.5 at 480), not at γ≤0.5. θ stayed below r=0.3. CPSP-8 lost layer-wise RMSE to dedicated models. Conclusions. γ is a bounded, pipeline-sensitive cross-task scalar, not a biomarker. Family-level precision-weighting identity holds in silico only when gain is large. Other decision parameters are mode switches; the OU layer remains frozen.
